brief.summary: A theory-of-change and logic-model composer for small nonprofit teams, where staff lay out how their inputs, activities, outputs and outcomes connect and attach evidence and indicators to each piece for funders.
brief.user: Marisol Vega, development director at Page Forward, a nine-person youth literacy nonprofit in Albuquerque that pays for the tool from its operations budget. She's put together several logic models before in word processors and hated keeping the arrows straight; the program director and the evaluation consultant also edit in the same workspace.
brief.moment: The McCune Foundation's full proposal is due Friday, and their reviewer asked for a revised theory of change that shows how the new summer 'Book Bridges' program connects to the existing after-school tutoring. Marisol is in the middle of restructuring the model: she just split the old 'Family engagement' activity into two separate activities, needs to rewire which outcomes each one feeds, move the new summer program's pieces in alongside the tutoring pieces without making them all cross over each other, rewrite two outcome statements so they're measurable, and resolve a comment from the evaluator saying one long-term outcome has no indicator.
brief.data: Model 'Page Forward ToC – v4 (McCune draft)', last edited by Dr. Ken Ishida (evaluator) 2 hours ago. 31 elements: 5 inputs (e.g., '42 trained volunteer tutors', 'APS partnership MOU'), 8 activities (e.g., 'Twice-weekly 1:1 tutoring, grades 2–4', 'Summer book-bag home visits'), 7 outputs (e.g., '180 students tutored per year', '2,400 books distributed'), 7 short/mid-term outcomes, 4 long-term outcomes (e.g., 'Increase share of participants reading at grade level by end of 3rd grade'). 38 connections between elements, 3 of them flagged by Ken as 'weak evidence'. Each outcome can hold indicators (e.g., 'iStation ISIP score, fall vs. spring', target +15 percentile points) and evidence citations (2 research studies, 1 internal 2025 evaluation report). 4 assumptions and 2 external factors noted along the edges ('Families have stable addresses over summer'). 6 open comments from 3 teammates. Version history v1–v4 since August.

prompt:
I need the front end for Throughline. A theory-of-change and logic-model composer for small nonprofit teams, where staff lay out how their inputs, activities, outputs and outcomes connect and attach evidence and indicators to each piece for funders.

Who's using it: Marisol Vega, development director at Page Forward, a nine-person youth literacy nonprofit in Albuquerque that pays for the tool from its operations budget. She's put together several logic models before in word processors and hated keeping the arrows straight; the program director and the evaluation consultant also edit in the same workspace.

What they're doing right now: The McCune Foundation's full proposal is due Friday, and their reviewer asked for a revised theory of change that shows how the new summer 'Book Bridges' program connects to the existing after-school tutoring. Marisol is in the middle of restructuring the model: she just split the old 'Family engagement' activity into two separate activities, needs to rewire which outcomes each one feeds, move the new summer program's pieces in alongside the tutoring pieces without making them all cross over each other, rewrite two outcome statements so they're measurable, and resolve a comment from the evaluator saying one long-term outcome has no indicator.

What's in the system at this point: Model 'Page Forward ToC – v4 (McCune draft)', last edited by Dr. Ken Ishida (evaluator) 2 hours ago. 31 elements: 5 inputs (e.g., '42 trained volunteer tutors', 'APS partnership MOU'), 8 activities (e.g., 'Twice-weekly 1:1 tutoring, grades 2–4', 'Summer book-bag home visits'), 7 outputs (e.g., '180 students tutored per year', '2,400 books distributed'), 7 short/mid-term outcomes, 4 long-term outcomes (e.g., 'Increase share of participants reading at grade level by end of 3rd grade'). 38 connections between elements, 3 of them flagged by Ken as 'weak evidence'. Each outcome can hold indicators (e.g., 'iStation ISIP score, fall vs. spring', target +15 percentile points) and evidence citations (2 research studies, 1 internal 2025 evaluation report). 4 assumptions and 2 external factors noted along the edges ('Families have stable addresses over summer'). 6 open comments from 3 teammates. Version history v1–v4 since August.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
